summary: Focused test of the new per-team data isolation commit (backend + frontend). Created /app/backend/tests/test_team_isolation.py (19 tests) covering registration->new team + default seeding, login teamId, events/times/standards/athletes scoping, cross-team read/update/delete denial, bulk-standards replace filter scoping, dedupe scoping, /api/seed idempotency, share-link scoping, and session-header fallbacks. Full backend suite: 97/97 passed (also fixed a broken BASE_URL in the pre-existing test_team_sharing.py which made 11 tests error out). Frontend verified with Playwright: registration creates team_5, session headers are sent on /api/seed, /api/events, /api/standards, /api/times, /api/athletes, and the new team sees only its own 24 seeded events with 0 standards/times/athletes from team1. Functional isolation works. However, isolation is NOT a security boundary: teamId is taken from an unsigned client-supplied X-User-Session header, so an unauthenticated caller can read and write ANY team's data by forging the header (verified with curl).

critical.issue: teamId is read from an unsigned, unverified client header (get_session/get_team_id). Verified: `curl -H 'X-User-Session: {"teamId":"team_5"}' /api/events` returned all 24 of team_5's events with no credentials, and an anonymous POST /api/standards with the same forged header inserted a record into team_5 (200). Any user can read/modify/delete another team's events, times, standards and athletes. Data isolation is display-only, not enforced.

minor.issue: Cross-team guard at line 540 requires `session and session.get('teamId')`. A caller with no session (or a session lacking teamId) is treated as team1 and the entry is silently stamped with the athlete's team, so anonymous callers can write time entries into any team.

Legacy docs in the alternate `db.times` collection are unconditionally stamped teamId='team1' (line 50) while `timeEntries` are derived from the athlete's team. GET /api/times then migrates those `times` docs into timeEntries, potentially mis-attributing legacy rows to team1.

teamId is derived as f'team_{user_id}' where user_id = max(existing id)+1. If a user row is ever removed, the id (and thus teamId) is reused and the new account inherits the previous team's leftover events/standards/times. Prefer a uuid-based team id.
Client-supplied `teamId` in RegisterRequest is accepted verbatim, so anyone can register directly into an existing team (e.g. teamId='team1') and gain full access to its data.
Event ids are deterministic (e_{teamId}_{idx}) with no unique index; two concurrent /api/seed calls for a new team can create duplicate events (the count-based guard is not atomic).

ui_bugs.issue: No data-testid attributes on any auth input/button (blocked automation). Added login-email-input, login-password-input, login-submit-button, login-error, demo-login-{name}, go-to-register-button, register-name/email/password inputs, register-role-select, register-submit-button, register-error, go-to-login-button.

integration_issues.issue: getSessionHeaders sends the entire User object as JSON, which for demo/mock users includes the plaintext `password` field (verified in request headers: '..."email":"alex@team.com","pas...'). Send only {userId, teamId, role} (or better, a signed token).
Frontend reads `error.error` but FastAPI returns `{detail: ...}`, so the 409 duplicate-email message is replaced by the generic 'Registration failed.' text.
All fetches use relative '/api/...' instead of process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (works behind ingress but violates the env-var contract).

issues: Tailwind CDN (cdn.tailwindcss.com) is loaded at runtime and logs a production warning; should be built via PostCSS

action_items: CRITICAL: stop trusting the client-supplied X-User-Session header. Resolve teamId server-side from an authenticated session/token (or at minimum validate userId+teamId against db.users) before scoping any query.
Reject or ignore client-supplied teamId in POST /api/auth/register (or gate it behind an invite code).
Tighten POST /api/times: reject writes when there is no valid session instead of falling back to team1/athlete team.
Frontend: send only {userId, teamId, role} in X-User-Session - the current payload leaks the demo users' plaintext password.
Frontend: read error messages from `detail` (FastAPI) so 409/400 messages surface on login/register.
Use uuid-based team ids instead of team_{sequential user id} to avoid team id reuse.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2237 lines - split into routers (auth, events, times, standards, teams, ai) and a db module.
get_session() swallows all exceptions with a bare `except:` and silently degrades to team1; log and/or 400 on malformed headers.
backfill_team_ids() runs at import time on every worker start; make it a startup event guarded by a migration marker document.
GET /api/times and GET /api/standards perform write migrations (copy from db.times/db.standards) inside read endpoints - move this to the migration path.
seed_data_creation: Registered 5 temporary users (TEST_iso_*, TEST_ui*) creating teams team_1..team_5; all users, their 24 seeded events, standards, times and athletes were deleted after testing. team1 data left untouched (7 events, 7 standards, 3 times, 3 athletes). 0 documents remain without a teamId.
test_credentials: Demo mock users (frontend only): alex@team.com / maria@parent.com / sarah@team.com / admin@swim.com, password123, all teamId=team1. DB users created for tests were cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Per-team scoping is functionally correct for every endpoint tested; do not re-test the happy path. The open item is authorization: teamId comes from the unsigned X-User-Session header, so forged headers grant full cross-team read/write (repro: curl -H 'X-User-Session: {"teamId":"<other team>"}' <BASE>/api/events). Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_team_isolation.py after the fix - the tests build headers via hdr(team_id) and will need real auth tokens once server-side session validation lands. Frontend localStorage session key is 'sq_prod_session_v3'.
rca_of_the_issue: get_team_id(get_session(x_user_session)) parses the raw X-User-Session header as JSON and uses its teamId with no verification against db.users and no signature, and defaults to 'team1' when absent. Mongo queries are therefore scoped by an attacker-controlled value, giving isolation for honest clients only.
